title.narrative: ILO Advancing the Decent Work Agenda in northern Africa - 2018-2025
ILO Advancing the Decent Work Agenda in northern Africa - 2018-2025

description.narrative:
Denna insats (Advancing the Decent Work Agenda in Northern Africa) är ett samarbete mellan Sida och International Labour Organisation ILO. Syftet är främja agendan för anständiga arbetsvillkor i Nordafrika. Insatsen bygger på en innovativ strategi för att främja bevisbaserad arbetsmarknadspolitik för full sysselsättning och effektiv tillgång till sociala och arbetstagarrättigheter i regionen. Insatsen ligger i linje med den svenska regeringens MENA-strategi 2016-20 (förbättrade möjligheter för regional ekonomisk utveckling som en förutsättning för fattiga människor att kunna förbättra sina levnadsvillkor) resultatområdet som berör ökad samverkan mellan länderna och arbetsmarknadens parter att verka för anständiga arbetsvillkor med fokus på social dialog och rättigheter. Insats är riktad mot länderna i Nordafrika; Marocko, Tunisien, och Egypten Internationella arbetsorganisationen (ILO) är FN:s fackorgan för sysselsättnings- och arbetslivsfrågor. ILO har som grundläggande mål att bekämpa fattigdom och befrämja social rättvisa. I uppgifterna ligger att främja sysselsättning och bättre arbetsvillkor i hela världen, samt att värna om fackliga rättigheter.ILO:s konstruktion bygger på att sammanföra regeringar med arbetstagare och arbetsgivare i en trepartisk institutionell struktur. På så sätt kan man hantera normbildning, motverka konflikter och lösa tvister med fredliga medel. Trepartsstrukturen är ILO:s unika kännemärke. Det är den enda FN-organisationen där, utöver regeringarna, aktörer i det civila samhället deltar som fullvärdiga beslutande parter i såväl styrelse som det högsta beslutande organet (Internationella arbetskonferensen, ILC).
Sida har en lång tradition av samarbete med ILO, både på global nivå men också kopplat till MENA-strategin

The aim of the intervention is to create better conditions for the job market and creation of new jobs. This is done by supporting effective implementation of international norms and regulations in the labor market - better apply the necessary labor market reforms and decisions that promote long-term sustainable job creation mechanisms. Here, issues like social protection, decent wages, dialogue between different partners in the labor market become central. The proposed intervention addresses many of the structural causes of today's labor market. The countries in the region have ratified several of the ILO Conventions but lack implementation. This effort aims to address and reduce the gap between ratification and implementation of international conventions, in order to create better conditions for people to get decent jobs. In addition, the ILO will support the countries with adequate and relevant evidence to implement appropriate labor market reforms

The Advancing the Decent Work Agenda in North Africa (ADWA) project aims to advance the Decent Work Agenda in North Africa. It is a five-year project (2018-2023), which takes an innovative approach to promote evidence-based policies for full employment and effective access to International Labour Standards (ILS), including at the workplace level.

The Advancing the Decent Work Agenda in North Africa project aims to promote job rich growth and International Labour Standards (ILS) and ensure their application at the enterprise level. These elements are fundamental for economic development and essential to making advancements towards the realization of Decent Work, as well as the Sustainable Development Goals in the three target countries: Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia.
The project managed to deliver on results despite the impact of the COVID-19 on the labour market. A number of highlighted results from 2022 are as follows:
- During the COVID-19 pandemic, in Egypt, Tunisia, and Morocco, multiple rounds of random digit dialling phone surveys were carried out targeting enterprises and households to assess the impact of COVID-19 on the labour market and provide policy recommendations for the tripartite constituents based on in-depth case studies. The surveys focussed on key labour market indicators such as employment and unemployment, wages and income, flexible working arrangements, household expenses and firms coping strategies, impacts on sales and revenues, respectively. The publications were completed with first-had data provided by the national statistical offices throughout the entire process.
- In Morocco, the project supported the Ministry of Economic Inclusion, Small Business, Employment and Skills (MIEPEEC) by digitizing more than 70 of its processes and procedures to strengthen its functional and organizational capacities so that it can function better internally, better perform its functions and also better serve citizens. Thus, 4 of the main directorates of this ministry have seen their processes and procedures digitized with a view to improving the overall management capacities of the ministry. This will contribute to the modernization of the MIEPEEC and the improvement of the services provided to citizens. The platform is expected to fully go live in mid-2023.
- In Egypt, in the framework of ADWA work on the promotion of ILS, the project established a close collaboration with the National Centre for Judicial Studies (NCJS), which is the training institute of the Ministry of Justice. Based on this, an agreement was reached to add a component on ILS to the essential annual training programme organized for the newly recruited judges. As a result, more than 600 judges were briefed on ILS and their application vis-à-vis the national legislation. In cooperation with the NCJS, the project also organized five rounds of workshops on Gender in Labour Law for 148 labour specialized judges from Primary Courts with a view to better address gender roles in jurisprudence.
- In Tunisia, ADWA project mainstreamed social dialogue and tripartism through: The development, tripartite endorsement and dissemination of the first diagnostic study on the ratification and implementation of ILS in Tunisia, which led to the ratification of the Promotional Framework for Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 2006 (No. 187) in 2021 that is now considered a fundamental Convention. Furthermore, in the framework of the cooperation agreement concluded between the ADWA' Project, and the Institut Supérieur de Magistrature (ISM), 24 labour judges (80% of the totality) took part to a training which provided them with a better understanding of the role of the ILO and introduced them to ILS. The workshop generated a great deal of satisfaction among Tunisian labour judges, 70% of whom were women, confirming their intention to make effective use of their improved knowledge of ILS in future judicial decisions.
